parts.note: the main or leading performer is the star
a swell is a dandy or posh person, a toff

explanation.surface: A great ocean wave starting to roll forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like the sea and 'swell' like a wave, but they are an adjective for leading and a noun for a posh gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb meaning to set out or get going on a journey or activity.

parts.note: a split within a religious body into opposing factions

explanation.walkthrough: 'division' suggests a department or diocese, but here it means a split.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal split within a religious body, as in the Great split of 1054.

parts.note: usually knocked over, but here dispatched by aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent flying' means knocked over in everyday speech; the exclamation hints at a letter posted by air.
explanation.definitionFit: Post dispatched by aeroplane is literally sent through the air.

indicators.note: must invade means the word we goes inside the word for hill

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A call to storm a hilltop fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall fortified building, like the keep of a castle or the Tower of London.

indicators.note: report means a spoken account, so the class name is said out loud

parts.note: in a school streamed A, B, C, the third stream of year four is form 4C

explanation.surface: Predicting a school report for a lower-set class.
explanation.walkthrough: British schools name forms by year and stream, so 4C is the third-ability group in the fourth year; said aloud it is 'four-see'.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate events is to predict or expect them beforehand.

clue.text: Beat in run to hospital, exploding myth

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: an exploded word is blown apart and its letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone rushes to hospital while debunking a legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link; the definition is 'Beat', a noun for musical pulse rather than a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A beat is the regular pulse or metre of music, its pattern of stresses.

parts.note: jump means hop
to scotch is to put an end to a rumour or plan

explanation.surface: A leap that finishes the match.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's playground pastime of hopping through chalked squares.

clue.text: A word for currency's ups and downs

definitions.text: A word for currency's ups and downs

parts.words: A word for currency's ups and downs
parts.note: currency looks like money, but here it is the flow of water currents that rise and fall

explanation.surface: Describing fluctuations in a money's value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currency' suggests exchange rates; read it as water currents rising and falling with the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for the regular rise and fall of the sea's ebb and flow.

clue.text: Notice serviceman outside in a pickle

indicators.note: outside means the serviceman wraps around the word for notice

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving at sea
an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: A soldier caught in an awkward predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a pickle' looks like the idiom for trouble; 'in' is a link and 'a pickle' is a seasoned soaking liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are seasoned liquids, such as vinegar brine, in which food is soaked before cooking.

clue.text: Computer equipment difficult to wear out

parts.note: difficult means hard

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters of wear are rearranged

explanation.surface: Computer kit that is tough to wear out.
explanation.definitionFit: The physical machinery and components of a computer, as opposed to its software programs.

indicators.note: hurt means damaged, so the letters of the fodder are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cricket leg-spin bowler's pride is wounded after a bad over.
explanation.walkthrough: A leg-spinner in cricket is a bowler who spins the ball from leg side; here it is a creature with legs that spins webs. The S of pride's counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description of an eight-legged arachnid that spins silk webs.

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: females means women

explanation.surface: Bare-chested ladies signal trouble ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent or foreboding sign of things to come, often ominous.

clue.text: Part of flight in latest aircraft

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words latest aircraft

explanation.surface: A section of an air journey aboard the newest plane.
explanation.walkthrough: A flight is also a set of steps, which is what 'flight' means here.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps is made up of individual treads, each one a single step.

parts.note: semi- is the prefix meaning half
the colon is an organ of the digestive tract

explanation.surface: Asks whether a single organ stop could be split in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ stop' suggests a pipe organ's knob; split it and 'stop' is a punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Punctuation marks used to be called stops, and this one makes a pause between full stop and comma.

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so the word for entreaties is said out loud

parts.note: entreaties are pleas, earnest requests

explanation.surface: Spoken appeals win approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To find favour with someone is to delight or satisfy them.

clue.text: One hoping not to miss the post, wanting endless fruit one cannot supply

definitions.text: One hoping not to miss the post

indicators.note: endless means the word for fruit loses its last letter

parts.note: an apple is a fruit
one cannot becomes I can't, with I for one

explanation.surface: Someone lacking fruit worries about missing the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the post' suggests the mail, but it is a job being applied for.
explanation.definitionFit: A job candidate hopes to secure, not lose, the position sought.

clue.text: Nicked when seen around the church

indicators.note: around means the word for seen surrounds the church abbreviation

parts.note: seen means noted, observed
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone is caught stealing when spotted near the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicked' suggests stolen or arrested, but here it means cut with small marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe having a small cut or indentation made in an edge.

clue.text: Workers given fish — a gesture of goodwill

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as in farm hands
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Staff receive a fish as a friendly present.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking palms is a greeting expressing friendship or agreement.

indicators.note: in means the award abbreviation sits inside the word for force

parts.note: to force is to coerce
MM is the Military Medal, a British gallantry award

explanation.surface: A company's prize is now in effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade, the buying and selling of goods, is business activity.

definitions.meaning: the psychoanalytic complex named by Freud for a son's desire for his mother
the mythical ruler of Thebes who unknowingly killed his father and married his mother

explanation.surface: A tangled story about a Theban monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud named his complex after the Greek tragic hero who ruled Thebes.

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A singer hits a bad note.
explanation.definitionFit: To warble is to trill or carol melodically, like a songbird.

clue.text: Ancient Greeks were riddled by it

definitions.text: Ancient Greeks were riddled by it

parts.words: Ancient Greeks were riddled by it
parts.note: riddled usually means full of holes, but here the Thebans were set riddles by a monster

explanation.surface: Something that left the old Greeks full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: In myth, the winged creature at Thebes asked travellers a riddle and devoured those who failed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythical lion-bodied creature famous for posing a riddle to Thebans.

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer's chosen dish is fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like a request to a waiter; the S of diner's counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oily fish of the herring family, often tinned.

clue.text: He flies automatically, some swear by him

definitions.meaning: pilots' slang name for an aircraft's autopilot

explanation.surface: A trusted automatic pilot that people vouch for.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen nicknamed the autopilot with this name, also heard in the old oath.

clue.text: After the battle, almost disregard the priest

indicators.note: after places the shortened word for disregard behind the battle

parts.note: Mons in Belgium was the site of a famous 1914 battle

indicators.note: almost means the word for disregard loses its final letter

parts.note: to disregard is to ignore

explanation.surface: Once the fighting ends, nearly overlook the clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last E of IGNORE, giving IGNOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A title given to senior Roman Catholic clergy, so a churchman or priest.

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters of nerve are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone's courage has failed, and denying it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean at no time or in no way whatsoever.

clue.text: Beer is found in the passage

indicators.note: found in means the word is sits inside the word for beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Beer spotted in a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkway between rows of seats or shelves, a narrow passageway.

clue.text: Unpleasant smell in craft — cancel space flight

indicators.note: in means the smell abbreviation sits inside the word for craft

parts.note: craft means skill, art
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A foul odour in the spacecraft forces the mission to be called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like the spaceship but means skill.
explanation.definitionFit: To call off a rocket mission before completion is to terminate it.

indicators.note: works means the letters are worked into a new arrangement, like a lever being operated

explanation.surface: A demonstration of how a lever operates.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to disclose or uncover it.

clue.text: Is around? That's odd, it disappeared a long time ago

definitions.text: it disappeared a long time ago

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters of is around are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: Someone puzzled that a long-vanished thing seems still around.
explanation.definitionFit: Prehistoric reptile that went extinct about sixty-six million years back.

parts.note: a list in a book of mistakes with the right versions to be read instead

explanation.walkthrough: 'readings' sounds like remedial reading lessons, but these are corrected passages in a printed text.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin plural for printed mistakes, listed with their corrections.

clue.text: He appreciates the exquisite tea these provide

indicators.note: provide here means the letters of tea these supply, once rearranged, the answer

explanation.surface: A connoisseur enjoys fine tea served here.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with refined sensitivity to beauty and art.
